techniques.comment: Credential dumping tools, including Mimikatz, are used to extract credentials from memory, enabling privilege escalation and lateral movement.
Remote access services such as RDP and VPNs are leveraged by affiliates for direct network access, often following credential compromise or brute-force activity.

LockBit affiliates exploit vulnerable internet-facing services and applications, including VPNs and web services, to gain unauthorized access to victim networks.
LockBit affiliates exfiltrate sensitive data using web-based file transfer services to facilitate double extortion operations prior to encryption.
Cloud storage services are abused for staging and exfiltration of stolen data, enabling large-scale data theft while blending with legitimate traffic.
SMB and Windows administrative shares are leveraged for lateral movement, allowing affiliates to propagate ransomware and access networked systems.
Desktop wallpapers and system visuals are modified to display ransom messaging and LockBit branding, reinforcing extortion pressure on victims.
Command-line interfaces are used by LockBit affiliates to execute payloads, automate tasks, and manage post-exploitation activity across compromised hosts.
PowerShell is leveraged for execution of malicious commands, system reconnaissance, payload delivery, and evasion by blending with legitimate administrative activity.
Observed in LockBit affiliate campaigns where phishing emails are used to deliver malicious attachments or links, enabling initial foothold through user interaction.
Affiliates frequently abuse compromised credentials, including those obtained from access brokers, to authenticate to victim systems and evade initial security controls.
